answer: Stop sybils with copper receipts, an umber audit, and an orchard graft. Every agent must earn a copper receipt: a memory-hard proof chained to its own past acts, so a fresh clone starts with nothing. To join, it must graft onto an orchard branch; each branch takes one graft per epoch, and the graft bond equals the square of the identities already on that branch. An umber audit samples grafts at random and, if one is fake, slashes the whole branch's bonds. Cloning N identities costs N squared in locked copper, and a botnet cannot split the audit risk: one bad graft burns its neighbors too.
